bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to local government; banning local elected officials from entering certain nondisclosure agreements; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 471.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[471.372] NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENTS.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Data center" has the meaning given in section 216B.02, subdivision 11.

(c) "Local elected official" means a member of a city council, mayor, county commissioner, watershed district manager, town supervisor, and any other elected official established by a home rule charter.

Subd. 2.

Nondisclosure agreements restricted.

(a) A local elected official must not enter into a nondisclosure agreement or other contract restricting public disclosure of information about a potential data center development within the boundaries of the political subdivision represented by the official.

(b) Any agreement or contract or term of an agreement or contract that violates paragraph (a) is void and unenforceable.

(c) When a contract contains a provision that is void and unenforceable under paragraph (b), that provision must be severed from the other provisions of the contract to the extent that it is void and unenforceable. The fact that the provision is void and unenforceable does not affect the other provisions of the contract.

(d) If a local elected official enters a contract or agreement that violates paragraph (a), the official must publicly disclose the contract or agreement.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to agreements entered into on or after that date.
